customer_name: Clerk of the Superior Court in Maricopa County
business_problem: The Clerk's Office was handling large volumes of time-sensitive citizen inquiries, and staff were losing time to repetitive calls, transfers and routine questions instead of focusing on more complex work.
solution_summary: The Clerk of the Superior Court in Maricopa County built Cleo, a virtual assistant powered by IBM watsonx Assistant, to centralize self-service support for citizens and staff. The project evolved from internal ChatOps experiments into an enterprise-grade conversational system that could survive beyond its original creator and be maintained by non-specialists. Watsonx Assistant became the operational core, giving the Clerk's Office a natural-language interface that could interpret requests, answer high-volume questions and route people without dead ends across existing customer-service channels. The design goal was not just to deflect calls, but to provide fair and timely access to public services such as record requests, marriage licenses and passport renewals even when employees were not physically present. By shifting routine inquiries to Cleo, the office created a scalable public-service support layer that reduced call burden and improved service continuity.

solution_components.name: IBM watsonx Assistant
solution_components.role: Runs the Cleo virtual assistant that interprets user questions, serves answers and routes citizens through self-service support flows.

data_flow: Citizen and employee questions enter Cleo through customer-service channels, watsonx Assistant interprets intent and returns an answer or guided next step, and unresolved requests are routed onward instead of forcing callers to restart the process.
business_outcome: Cleo now handles a large share of incoming demand, saving staff time every month while letting the office offer faster, more consistent support to citizens without making agents pause complex work to answer routine calls.
architecture_clues: The project grew out of internal ChatOps experiments before moving to a managed conversational platform.
The office prioritized maintainability by nontechnical staff as a key design constraint.
The deployment is intended to avoid dead ends by answering or routing requests instead of restarting the support journey.
